content_of_post_to_comment:
After plentiful ruts where the only thing I do is go to work , go home play videogames, and live like that’s what I’ll do for the rest of my life.

I’ve gotten back “on the horse” - the horse being what I feel it takes to chase after my goal of creating a more financially comfortable life for myself where I have the confidence I could financially support myself ( motivation, inspiration, executive function, etc.)

Problem I’ve felt this way before and many times it just ends up with me crashing and burning. Studying feels jarring, if I’m not playing videogames im gonna go to sleep, I stop exercising and dieting, etc. and just generally go through the motions of life

This can last for years.

Well I’m out of that rut right now and I’d really like to ride this wave into a better position but I don’t know how I’ll ward off the burnout this time. I hope it doesn’t come back, but it has a track record of coming back.
comment: I wonder if part of the burnout comes from treating these motivated periods like a window where you have to fix everything before the motivation disappears. Maybe studying, exercising, and eating better all at once becomes exhausting. It might be worth deliberately doing less than you feel capable of right now, just to build a routine you can still maintain on the days when you genuinely don't feel like doing anything.
